editorial:
Imagine being the guy everyone goes to for advice on how to get over a tragedy, but you can't even fix your own life. That is the deal with Burke, a self-help guru who tells thousands of people how to move on while he is still secretly heartbroken over his late wife. He has a polished public image, but inside, he is totally stuck. Then he meets Eloise, a spunky florist who doesn't buy into his perfect act. She is the kind of person who pushes him out of his comfort zone and forces him to actually deal with his pain instead of just talking about it in a book. The vibe is sweet, emotional, and feels like a warm hug on a rainy day.

You will love the chemistry between the leads because it feels real and not forced. The pacing is steady, though some parts feel a bit like a typical romance novel. The best part is seeing Burke finally break down and be honest with himself. If you want a good cry and a happy ending, you should definitely check this out. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best picture, or if you prefer owning your movies, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great move. It is a perfect pick for a cozy movie night with a partner.
endingExplained: In the end, Burke finally stops hiding behind his books and faces his grief head-on. He realizes that loving Eloise does not mean he is betraying his late wife. The movie wraps up with Burke and Eloise choosing to be together and start a new chapter. He finds a balance between honoring his past and embracing his future, giving the story a hopeful and heartwarming conclusion that leaves you feeling good.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves heartfelt stories about second chances and healing from loss.
